direction_basis: hypocalcaemia and hypercalcaemia are both pathological
hypophosphataemia and hyperphosphataemia are both pathological
hypertension is the disease axis; hypotension is not scored in this ambulatory cohort
same hypertension disease axis as systolic pressure
high pulse reflects sympathetic overdrive or poor fitness; the low tail is clinically ambiguous without fitness or rhythm data
lymphopenia and lymphocytosis are both adverse
neutropenia and neutrophilia are both adverse
high monocytes reflect myeloid skew and inflammaging; the low tail is not an ageing deficit
eosinophilia is adverse; the near-zero lower tail is not meaningful
basophilia is adverse; the near-zero lower tail is not meaningful
low globulin can reflect immunodeficiency or hepatic dysfunction and high globulin inflammation or paraproteinaemia
high blood urea nitrogen reflects azotaemia; the low tail is not scored as renal ageing
hyperuricaemia is adverse; low urate is not scored
hypoalbuminaemia reflects inflammatory or hepatic dysfunction; high albumin commonly reflects dehydration
high alanine aminotransferase reflects hepatocellular injury
high aspartate aminotransferase reflects hepatocellular or muscle injury
hyperbilirubinaemia is adverse; low bilirubin is not scored
high lactate dehydrogenase reflects tissue damage haemolysis or malignancy
high gamma-glutamyl transferase reflects cholestasis or alcohol-related injury
high alkaline phosphatase reflects cholestatic or bone pathology
high glycated haemoglobin is the dysglycaemic disease axis
high waist-to-height ratio reflects central adiposity
high cholesterol is atherogenic while low cholesterol can accompany frailty occult disease or hepatic dysfunction
low HDL cholesterol is adverse; high HDL is not scored
hypertriglyceridaemia is adverse
thrombocytopenia and thrombocytosis are both adverse
both tails can reflect abnormal platelet production
anaemia and polycythaemia are both adverse
microcytosis and macrocytosis are both adverse
low MCHC reflects hypochromia while high MCHC can reflect red-cell pathology
high red-cell distribution width reflects anisocytosis; the low tail is not meaningful
low red-cell folate reflects folate deficiency; the high tail is not scored
hyponatraemia and hypernatraemia are both adverse
hypokalaemia and hyperkalaemia are both adverse
hypochloraemia and hyperchloraemia can reflect acid-base pathology
low and high bicarbonate can reflect acidosis and alkalosis respectively
high albumin-creatinine ratio reflects albuminuria
low estimated glomerular filtration rate reflects chronic kidney disease
